assumption: Users will pay for a cross-vertical opportunity workflow before they trust full automation.
why_it_matters: Determines whether the MVP can monetize without auto-submit risk.
how_to_test: Sell a concierge-plus-dashboard pilot to 10-15 users.
pass_criteria: At least 3 users pay or pre-commit after a manual pilot.

assumption: Funded international mobility has stronger repeat usage than generic job search.
why_it_matters: Justifies the wedge and shapes data ingestion priorities.
how_to_test: Track whether users return weekly for deadlines and new matches.
pass_criteria: 50% of pilot users engage in 3 or more weekly sessions.

assumption: A human-in-the-loop application workspace is enough to create value before autonomous submission exists.
why_it_matters: Avoids premature trust and policy risk.
how_to_test: Measure saved time and submission completion rates with assisted workflows.
pass_criteria: Median application-prep time falls by at least 50%.

assumption: Cross-vertical scoring can outperform raw directories in shortlist quality.
why_it_matters: Core reason op2u exists instead of being a content business.
how_to_test: Compare manual expert shortlist vs op2u-scored shortlist on user acceptance.
pass_criteria: Users accept 60% or more of top-10 scored opportunities.

assumption: Official-source routing plus structured extraction can keep trust high enough despite aggregator skepticism.
why_it_matters: Trust is a gating factor for any opportunity product.
how_to_test: Show source transparency in pilot and survey perceived trust.
pass_criteria: Average trust rating 4/5 or higher from pilot users.
